summary: The frozen history test rejected every pre-registered stock rule: each beat only a small share of random baskets from the same list, and holding every name equally beat every rule and the core. Setup checks and past strength have shown no edge here. The market rallied hard on the latest day, but one strong day does not end a stressed downtrend. All five calls stay neutral with low conviction. Nothing here is expected to beat the index; real money stays in the whole-market plan.
eli5: After a tired week, almost every runner sprinted on the latest day. The brain still does not guess who keeps going, because guessing did no better than luck before. It watches with pretend money, and the family's real money keeps going into the whole-market basket every week.
letter:
Dear family,

First, real money. This week's buy of the whole-market fund goes in as usual, if it has not already. Nothing to sell. The market jumped on the latest day, and that is no more a reason to rush in than last week's fall was a reason to run. Money we may need soon stays safe.

Second, the pretend game. Every stock rule we wrote down in advance lost to baskets picked at random from the same list, so our stock calls stay neutral. Last week's bet is on track to lose, which would leave the game at two won and two lost. A new bet starts this week. Luck alone wins about half the weeks.

Third, a lesson. Last week a fall, this week a leap. Big days in both directions tend to come close together when the market is nervous. Those who sold in the fall missed the leap.

Fourth, what would change our minds: a rule that beats random picks on history and then keeps a paper record ahead of the whole market for at least half a year. Until then we stay patient.

With care, the brain
